principles.title: Bound autonomy with invariants
principles.claim: Specify what must remain true, the capability boundary, and required evidence; leave agents freedom only inside that envelope.

principles.title: Separate proposer, executor, and evaluator
principles.claim: Intent, execution, and evaluation should remain independently inspectable even when one agent participates in all three.

principles.title: Make effects attributable and replayable
principles.claim: Consequential operations must leave enough durable evidence to reconstruct authority, starting state, attempted effect, result, and completion check.

principles.title: Test the test
principles.claim: A verifier is not established until a controlled violation proves it can fail and recovery proves it can return to green.

principles.title: Treat boundary bytes as versioned commitments
principles.claim: A value another component stores, hashes, authorizes, parses, or verifies is a migration across a dependency graph—not a local string edit.

principles.title: Preserve provenance and publish corrections
principles.claim: Retain navigable evidence, record corrections beside original decisions, and update active rules without rewriting history to look prescient.

principles.title: Place each rule at the narrowest shared scope
principles.claim: Put an invariant at the nearest governance boundary shared by every component that must obey it.

principles.title: Distinguish proposed, observed, accepted, and committed state
principles.claim: Working-tree edits, local checks, commits, deployments, and observed production effects are different claims and must not collapse into done.

principles.title: Make exceptions explicit and load-bearing
principles.claim: Every exception should name the external fact requiring it, the risk of removal, and the event that permits retirement.

principles.title: Fix the source, not the adopter
principles.claim: When an owned shared component violates its declared contract, repair the defect there instead of encoding it as downstream architecture.

principles.title: Contain the failure, continue the safe frontier
principles.claim: Checkpoint blocked work and continue only independently verifiable safe tasks; uncertainty about consequential dependencies is itself a stop boundary.
